prompt:
A desktop web app screen, edge to edge, crisp readable text, no browser window, device or desk around it. Product: Hive, a team workspace where people chat in channels and one shared AI agent does tasks on its own computer. The visitor's job: see what the agent is doing, answer it, and review finished work before it goes out. Workspace: Fern & Fig (a plant shop). Channel list: launch, design, ops, hiring, plus Chat, Tasks, Files, Goals, Computer. Top bar: Hive bee mark with workspace name, a badge '2 need you', search, avatar.
The #launch channel is open: a short team chat on the left (Priya: 'Photos are in, hero is the maidenhair fern.'; Marcus: '@hive what do we still need before the send?' with the agent's reply). On the right a vertical task rail of tickets: an 'At the pass' section holding 'Write the launch email' (agent, ready for review, 18m, due Fri) with buttons Send and Send back; below it 'Set up the pre-order page' (agent, running, 42m), 'Order 8-inch boxes' (failed: supplier out of stock) and 'Brief support on pre-order questions' (Dana, to do). Composer at the bottom. Status-led: the rail is what the eye finds first.
Look: a restaurant pass. A committed brushed stainless cool-grey shell, white thermal-ticket paper cards with a torn top edge and a live age timer, condensed grotesque headings, tabular monospace for times and counts. Signal colours do jobs: fire orange running, green sent, red 86'd failed, amber hold for review. Everything else is clean standard web controls.
